analysis.title: Speculators Are Gunning For No Fed Hike In December
key_insights: Speculators and leveraged funds have sharply raised their net long in fed funds futures as a share of open interest, to the highest level since 2020 per CFTC Commitment of Traders data (latest data as of last Tuesday, published Friday). The author reads this as a bet on a lower policy rate than priced.
The market overall still prices almost a 75% chance of a Fed hike in December, so speculator positioning diverges from market pricing.

SOFR futures positioning remains net short. The author suggests part of this may be spread trades, since SOFR has widened versus fed funds as the Treasury's account at the Fed has grown, but suspects the main driver is views on tighter Fed policy expectations.

The author treats fed funds futures positioning as a cleaner read on speculators' Fed views than SOFR futures. SOFR futures extend further down the curve and are heavily used to hedge rate swaps, cross-currency swaps and other products.
Speculators' historical record on Fed outcomes, based on their positioning, shows no clear edge.
Given the market turmoil and what is at stake if the AI trade falters, the author judges a lower expected chance of a December Fed hike to be appropriate.

NDX is in correction, down over 10% from its highs. The SOX semiconductor index is down over 10% in two days to its lowest since April. Only 0.4% of days in its 32-year history posted a worse daily return than Friday's decline.

Hedge fund selling and rotation were named as the main drivers, as portfolio managers face mounting AI-related trade losses. Gold fell 5.4% on a day when yields and the dollar were lower, which the author reads as a market needing liquidity to cover losses and margin elsewhere.

sector_views.rationale: SOX is down over 10% in two days to its lowest since April, and NDX is in correction, amid hedge fund selling and AI-related trade losses. This is a description of price action, not an explicit sector recommendation.

SOFR futures positioning remains net short, in contrast to fed funds futures.
SOFR has widened versus fed funds as the size of the Treasury's account at the Fed has grown, which may account for part of the SOFR short through spread trades.
Hedge fund selling and rotation, tied to AI-related trade losses, are cited as the main drivers of the equity selloff.
Speculators' positioning has historically given no clear edge in predicting Fed policy.
